title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Cloak & Brooch of Lórien. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Cloak & Brooch of Lórien
options.lineage: The Fellowship's parting gifts: grey-green Elven cloaks and the enamel leaf brooch
options.thesis: A translator wearing the Lórien cloak: grey-green twilight panels, silver lettering, and each Elvish word set like an enamel leaf whose veins trace back to the English.
options.viewport: Top bar with Sindarin/Quenya tabs; English input left, the Elvish line large on the right in silver with Tengwar beneath; a word-by-word provenance strip below.
options.risk: Grey-green can go murky and sombre if the silver and enamel are timid.

raised.raise: Strict value economy: every tone carries a job (ground, panel, text, action, flag), no decorative grey.
Every word carries fixed furniture in fixed slots: gloss, part of speech, source, provenance.
Mallorn gold is reserved solely for non-canon Neo-Elvish words, so a fill-in is spotted at a glance.
Bright enamel green appears only where something can be pressed.

options.label: Ithildin
options.lineage: The moon-letters on the West-gate of Moria
options.thesis: Translations drawn as ithildin: silver-white lines that wake on dark stone when the phrase resolves.
options.viewport: Dark stone ground, English in a slim input up top, the Elvish phrase and Tengwar drawn in glowing line across a central arch.
options.risk: The most familiar LoTR look; dark-plus-glow is where most runs in this category land.

options.label: Star Atlas of Elbereth
options.lineage: Celestial star atlases; the Eldar as the star-folk
options.thesis: Every word is a star: its size is how strongly Tolkien attests it, and lines join the phrase like a constellation.
options.viewport: Navy field; input top-left; the Elvish phrase plotted as word-stars sized by attestation, glosses in small italic.
options.case: Fuses well: attestation-as-magnitude is a true provenance encoding and Elbereth resonates. Loses on clarity: a star plot reads slower than a line.
options.risk: Can turn a sentence into a puzzle if the plotted layer outranks the readable line.

options.label: The Editor's Apparatus
options.lineage: Wide-margin critical editions like The History of Middle-earth
options.thesis: English and Elvish as twin columns round a vermilion rail of word keys, sources hung in the margin like an editor's notes.
options.viewport: Two columns, English and Elvish, joined by a centre rail of numbered keys; the margin carries each word's source citation.
options.case: Fuses strongly on clarity: the apparatus IS provenance. Loses on audience identification: reads as a scholarly edition before a translator.
options.risk: Bone paper and serif is the category's default rendition; must stay razor sharp.

options.label: Datamatics
options.thesis: The lexicon as a strobing barcode field.
options.viewport: Barcode field with the phrase pulled into focus.
options.case: Fuses poorly: nothing in Tolkien's world reads as data-sublime.
options.risk: Cold and alien to the audience.
options.kept: Strict value economy: every tone has a job.

options.label: Character Goods Catalog
options.thesis: Words as a ranked roster of cute characters.
options.viewport: A pastel grid of word cards.
options.kept: Fixed furniture per entry: gloss, part of speech, source.

options.label: Boarding Pass & Gate Board
options.thesis: Translation as a ticket with a live board.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no link to the audience.
options.kept: One colour reserved strictly for what needs noticing (non-canon words).

options.label: Warm Consumer App
options.viewport: A card stack with a bottom bar.
options.case: Fuses blandly: loses all of Middle-earth.
options.kept: The bright colour appears only where something can be pressed.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean two-pane translator in the Google Translate mould, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Language pickers above two side-by-side text panes.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from any translator; Middle-earth is absent.
